defender.title: SharkNet Defender
defender.idle_sub: Start control to arm the ARP watchdog.
defender.protect_tip: Static ARP Lock — pin the gateway MAC so no one can spoof you
intel.policy_tip: Physical network is healthy; these are intentional SharkNet policies, not a network problem.
intel.policy_tip_load: Latency/loss on this PC is inflated by SharkNet's forwarding load, not a network fault.
devices.empty: Choose an adapter and start control to observe this LAN.
devices.select_tip: Select this device for bulk actions
devices.name_hint: Click to name this device — SharkNet remembers it
notif.new_device.title: New device detected
notif.device_offline.title: Device offline
notif.device_online.title: Device online
notif.cut.title: Device blocked
notif.cut.body: {name} has been cut from the network.
notif.hardcut.title: Hard Cut
notif.hardcut.body: {name} has been completely cut from the network.
notif.limit.title: Device limited
notif.security.title: Security alert
hardcut.tip: Maximum isolation — no forwarding, no monitoring
hardcut.note: Hard Cut completely isolates this device. Traffic monitoring is unavailable while Hard Cut is active.
info.pol_hardcut: HARD CUT by SharkNet — this device is fully isolated and, by design, not monitored.
visited.hardcut: This device is Hard Cut — fully isolated, so there is no traffic to inspect.
confirm.hardcut_selected_msg: Fully isolate {n} selected device(s)? They lose all network access and cannot be monitored.
monitor.label: Monitor
monitor.tip: Observe this device without blocking or limiting it
info.pol_cut: CUT by SharkNet — traffic is intentionally blocked here (this is a policy, not a network fault).
info.pol_limit: LIMITED by SharkNet — throughput is intentionally capped here (this is a policy, not a network fault).
services.hint: Click a service to block it for this device (covers its DNS, SNI & HTTP; QUIC best-effort). Click again to unblock.
services.restricted: Services can't be blocked for this device (self / gateway).
domains.disclaimer: Blocks DNS, visible TLS hostnames, and plain HTTP. VPNs, encrypted DNS (DoH), and ECH can bypass domain rules.
domains.restricted: Domains can't be blocked for this device (self / gateway).
visited.title: Visited sites
visited.hint: Sites this device was observed reaching — observation only. A site here is not blocked unless it shows a “blocked” tag.
visited.empty: No sites observed yet — traffic will appear here as it's seen.
visited.off: This device is not being monitored. Turn on Monitor to observe its traffic — it won't be blocked or limited.
visited.cut: This device is Cut — its traffic is blocked, so there's nothing to observe.
history.title: Traffic history
history.subtitle: last 10 min
history.empty: No history yet — apply LIMIT or CUT (or block a domain) to start recording this device.
network.title: Network-wide blocks
network.note: Applies to every device on the network — for this session only (cleared on Stop & restore). A network block overrides a device's ALLOW.
network.placeholder: block a domain for all devices
network.strip_tip: Applies to every device — cleared when you Stop control
confirm.cut_others_msg: Cut internet for ALL other devices — everyone except this PC and the gateway?
toast.others_restored_sub: All other devices set to Allow
speed.title: Speed test
speed.failed: Speed test failed — check your internet connection and try again.
speed.no_throughput: No throughput measured — the test host may be unreachable on this network.
speed.timeout: Speed test timed out — the network may be too slow or offline.
smac.title: SharkMAC — MAC Address Manager
smac.warn: Changing the MAC will reset the current SharkNet session. Active cuts and bandwidth limits will be cleared, and SharkNet will run a fresh scan.
smac.changing: Changing MAC — the adapter will reconnect (~10s)…
smac.restoring: Restoring original MAC — the adapter will reconnect (~10s)…
smac.session_reset: Your SharkNet network session has been reset. All active device cuts and bandwidth limitations have been cleared. A fresh network scan is now running.
smac.no_reset: This isn't the adapter SharkNet is controlling, so your current session was left untouched.
smac.need_mac: Generate or enter a MAC first.
smac.timeout: Timed out waiting for the adapter. It may not support this change.
about.title: About SharkNet
about.desc: SharkNet — network control & security. Discover, protect, and manage the devices on your own network.
about.disclaimer: For good & lawful use only. Use SharkNet only on networks you own or are authorized to manage — for parental control, bandwidth management, and protecting your own network. Do not use it to harm, spy on, or disrupt others. Use it for good.
about.dedication: In loving memory of my dear father
footer.dedication: In loving memory of my father · إهداء إلى روح والدي 🤍
advice.winpcap.title: WinPcap detected — please switch to Npcap
advice.winpcap.text: WinPcap (2013, unmaintained) is unreliable on Windows 10/11 and causes intermittent scans, lag, and weak LIMIT. Uninstall WinPcap and install Npcap for stable results.
advice.topology.title: No other devices found
advice.topology.text: Your phones/other devices are likely on a different router (behind NAT), which ARP can't reach. Connect this PC (by cable) to the SAME network your devices are on, then scan again.
settings.title: Settings
settings.background_desc: SharkNet can keep enforcing your rules while the window is closed.
settings.keep_running: Keep running in the background when I close the window
settings.keep_running_desc: Closing hides SharkNet in the system tray instead of quitting. Your rules stay active.
settings.minimize_to_tray_desc: Minimizing sends SharkNet to the tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.start_with_windows_desc: Adds SharkNet to this user's startup programs.
settings.tray_unavailable: The system tray is unavailable, so closing the window will quit SharkNet.
settings.notif_note: Notifications only report what SharkNet does — they never block, cut or limit anything by themselves.
settings.cat.new_device: A new device joins the network
status.background_tip_on: SharkNet keeps running in the system tray when you close the window.
status.background_tip_off: Closing the window stops SharkNet and restores every device.
smac.no_adapters: No Ethernet or Wi-Fi adapter available.
settings.runtime_note: Live status of the SharkNet runtime. Read-only.
settings.restore_rules_desc: Reapply your saved device rules when SharkNet starts.
settings.restore_rules_warn: Saved CUT and HARD CUT rules may disconnect devices as soon as SharkNet starts.
